purpose: General principles for writing design documents when no project rules exist: definition, prohibited content, quantitative targets, judgment criteria, structure, maintenance, norms and a severity catalog.
summary: Design document definition: responsibility is How, what it excludes, permanence and revision via additive development
Prohibited content: large source code, unjustified technology choices, features absent from requirements, guaranteed quantitative targets
Quantitative targets: describe structure and policy only, never guarantees or AI-guessed values
Judgment criterion: can an implementer implement from this; hierarchical splitting guidance
Optional sections, Mermaid diagram guidelines, and no history sections
Maintenance: report implementation-design divergence to the user and record design intent
Norms for architecture dependency direction, responsibility separation and cohesion, availability and SPOF, with gray-zone tolerances
Severity catalog covering prohibited content, deliverables, failure patterns, architecture and additive-feature frontmatter
tasks: Judging whether content belongs in design or requirements
Assigning severity to design review findings
Checking architecture dependency direction and responsibility split
Updating a design document after implementation changes
Splitting a large design document hierarchically
title: 設計書 作成原則
